description: Pipeline scope (pipeline-scope.sh, PermissionRequest) is the one command hook. For the scheduled pipeline only, marked by WORKBENCH_DEV_TEAM_PIPELINE=1 on the process bin/dispatch-agent.sh spawns, it allows a prompt for one plain git -C <dir>, rm, or rmdir command when every path is absolute and stays inside the roots: all of $TMPDIR, where every mktemp -d folder lands, so another run's clone is in scope too, and the scratch roots. The git subcommand must be add, checkout, commit, diff, log, merge, or push. It never allows a pull request merge, a force push, a push to the default branch, or a command a user deny rule matches. The hooks module (register.ts) holds the rest. It routes a dispatch of a dev-team agent to its mode agent, sets its model and effort from the config, adds the fan-out knobs to the prompt of Holmes and of Lestrade's Item mode, and refuses a main-session Watson brief whose bare Workdir sits on main, master, or trunk. It runs every helper Holmes spawns as holmes-lens. A main-session Watson Item ID call runs bin/dispatch-agent.sh in place of the spawn, and every other main-session dev-team dispatch runs in the background unless the call asked for the foreground. A dev-team agent's bare mktemp lands in a folder of its own under a scratch root, deleted when a turn of that agent ends with no live child, and a run past its 250k working-context budget is reported to the human once. A dev-team sub-agent cannot end its turn while a helper it spawned, or a background command it started, has not reported: SubagentStop refuses the turn end and tells it to keep making short tool calls. A helper that makes no model request or tool call, or a background command whose output file does not grow, across two refusals stops holding it, and is named so the agent reports it. On every Bash, Edit, Write, and NotebookEdit call it runs the review guard, which reads the command through workbench-core's $.workbench.parseShell and refuses a write outside the scratch roots by Holmes, his mode agents, his helper holmes-lens, or anything they spawned. It catches mistakes and is not a security boundary. It also draws two read-only panes: /dev-team-runs, the newest dispatched runs from the dispatch logs, and /dev-team-board, The Index's three lanes from bin/dispatch-tick.sh --board, fetched once per dispatch cadence at most.
